paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average change percentage in answer by turn number, comparing initial correct and incorrect answers. The x-axis represents turn number on a linear scale, ranging from 1 to 7, with tick labels at intervals of 1. The y-axis represents average change percentage on a linear scale, ranging from 0% to 50%, with tick labels at intervals of 10%. The line for initial correct answers is red, with a solid line style and circular markers; it starts at approximately 4% at turn 1 and increases to around 11% at turn 4, then remains steady at around 11% across turns 4 to 7. The line for initial incorrect answers is orange, with a solid line style and circular markers; it starts at approximately 16% at turn 1, increases to around 24% at turn 2, then to around 25% at turn 3, followed by a sharp increase to about 47% at turn 4, and remains steady at around 47% across turns 4 to 7.
